title: At Home and with Family
description: Ten short stories about home, family and simple everyday moments.

lessons.title: A New Home
lessons.summary: Sam, Anna and their daughter Lily have a new home in Ohio.
lessons.text:
Sam and Anna have a new home. It is in Dayton. Dayton is in the state of Ohio.

Sam and Anna have a daughter, Lily. Lily is 6.

Lily has a new room. She looks at it. She says: "This is my room! It is a good room!"

Anna says: "This is a new home, and it is a good one."

Sam says: "It is. It is a new home in a new state. And it is ours now."

Questions:
What do Sam and Anna have?
Sam and Anna have a new home.
What state is the new home in?
It is in the state of Ohio.
Who is Lily?
Lily is the daughter of Sam and Anna.
What does Lily have?
Lily has a new room.
What does Sam say?
Sam says: "It is a new home in a new state."

lessons.title: Max Is Not Here
lessons.summary: Ben looks for his dog Max and finds him out back.
lessons.text:
Ben has a dog, Max. Ben is 9, and Max is 4.

One day, Ben does not find Max. He says: "Max! Max!" Max does not come.

Ben looks in his room. Max is not there. He looks in the kitchen. Max is not there. He looks on his bed. No, Max is not on his bed.

Then Ben looks out back. There is Max! Max is out back, in the sun.

Ben says: "Max, there you are! Come here!" Max comes back in with Ben. Now Max is here with Ben.

Questions:
What does Ben have?
Ben has a dog, Max.
Does Ben find Max in his room?
No, Max is not there.
Is Max in the kitchen?
No, Max is not in the kitchen.
What does Ben find out back?
Ben finds Max out back.
What does Ben say?
Ben says: "Max, there you are! Come here!"

lessons.title: Flowers for Jane
lessons.summary: Emma finds flowers for her mother, Jane, and Jane likes them.
lessons.text:
Emma is 7. Her mother is Jane.

Emma thinks: "What does my mother like? I think she likes flowers. I want to give my mother some flowers."

Emma goes out. She finds one flower. It is a good one. She finds one more, and then one more. Now she has 3.

Emma gives them to Jane. She says: "These are for you. I think you like them."

Jane looks at them. She says: "I like them, Emma! What good flowers! I like them all."

Questions:
Who is Jane?
Jane is the mother of Emma.
What does Emma want to give Jane?
Emma wants to give Jane some flowers.
What does Emma think?
Emma thinks Jane likes flowers.
What does Emma find?
She finds 3 good flowers.
What does Jane say?
Jane says: "I like them, Emma!"

lessons.title: Two Cats
lessons.summary: Lucy and Jack have two cats, and each cat likes one of them more.
lessons.text:
Lucy and Jack have two cats, Tom and Mia. They are good cats.

Tom is one of the two cats. He is 9. Mia is the other one. She is only 2.

Tom likes Lucy. He also likes Jack, but he likes Lucy more than Jack. Tom is with Lucy all the time.

The other cat, Mia, also likes Lucy, but she likes Jack more than Lucy. Mia is with Jack all the time.

Which cat is the best? Lucy thinks it is Tom. Jack thinks it is Mia. They think their two cats are good cats.

Questions:
Who are Tom and Mia?
They are the two cats of Lucy and Jack.
Which cat is only 2?
Mia is only 2.
Which cat likes Lucy more than Jack?
Tom likes Lucy more than Jack.
Who does Mia like more?
Mia likes Jack more than Lucy.
Which cat does Lucy think is the best?
Lucy thinks it is Tom.
What do Lucy and Jack think of their cats?
They think their two cats are good cats.

lessons.title: A Cake with Leo
lessons.summary: Paul and Leo get some eggs and make a cake.
lessons.text:
Paul wants to make a cake with his son, Leo. Leo is 10.

First, they need some eggs. Leo looks for them. Are there any eggs? No, there are not any.

Paul says: "We need some eggs. I can get some." He goes out and gets 6 eggs. Then he comes back with them.

Now Paul and Leo make the cake. First, they use 3 of the eggs. Then they use some other things.

After some time, Leo says: "Is it time?" Paul looks at the cake. He says: "It is time!"

After that, Paul and Leo have some cake. It is so good! Leo says: "We can make one more some other time!"

Questions:
What do Paul and Leo want to make?
They want to make a cake.
What do they need first?
First, they need some eggs.
Are there any eggs?
No, there are not any.
What does Paul get?
He gets 6 eggs.
What do they use first?
First, they use 3 eggs.

lessons.title: Grandpa Joe
lessons.summary: Grandpa Joe comes from Texas to see his family one day a year.
lessons.text:
Kate and Nick have a grandpa, Joe. Joe is from Texas.

One day a year, Joe comes to see Kate and Nick. Today is that day.

A man comes to the door. The man is Joe! Nick says: "It is our grandpa!" Kate says: "Our grandpa is here!"

Joe comes in. Then other people come in, one by one. They are all from the family. Kate and Nick know all the people.

Joe says: "I know it is only one day a year. But it is a good day."

Kate says: "It is the best day of the year!"

Questions:
Who is Joe?
Joe is the grandpa of Kate and Nick.
What state is Joe from?
Joe is from Texas.
When does Joe come?
Joe comes one day a year.
Who comes in after Joe?
Other people from the family come in, one by one.
What does Kate say?
Kate says: "It is the best day of the year!"

lessons.title: Mike Goes to Work
lessons.summary: Mike gets up, goes to work, and comes back to his family.
lessons.text:
Mike gets up at 6. He has to go to work.

At 7, Mike goes out. He gets into his car. On the way to work, he thinks about his day.

At work, Mike works and works. He likes his work.

At 5, the work day is over. Now Mike can go back. He goes out and gets into his car. On the way back, he thinks of his family.

At 6, Mike comes in. His daughter, Rosie, says: "You are back!" Mike says: "I am back. Work is over now."

Questions:
When does Mike get up?
Mike gets up at 6.
When does Mike go out?
Mike goes out at 7.
What does Mike get into?
He gets into his car.
When is the work day over?
At 5, the work day is over.
What does Mike think of on the way back?
He thinks of his family.
What does Rosie say?
Rosie says: "You are back!"

lessons.title: The Family Picture
lessons.summary: Amy takes a picture of her family and their dog, Buddy.
lessons.text:
Liz and Dan have a daughter, Amy. They also have a dog, Buddy. Amy wants to take a picture of all the family.

Amy says: "Come here, all of you! Right here, with Buddy!" Liz and Dan come right over with Buddy.

Buddy has its ball. Buddy just looks at its ball. Amy says: "Buddy, look at me!" Buddy does not look. Then Dan says: "Buddy, look at Amy!" Now Buddy looks at Amy.

Amy says: "That is so good, Buddy! Now all of you, look at me!" They all look at Amy.

Amy takes the picture. She looks at it. She can see all of them well. She says: "That is so good! It is just right."

Questions:
What does Amy want?
Amy wants to take a picture of all the family.
What does Buddy look at?
Buddy looks at its ball.
What does Dan say?
Dan says: "Buddy, look at Amy!"
Can Amy see all of them well?
Amy can see all of them well.

lessons.title: Can You Do This with Me?
lessons.summary: Ella helps her brother Tom with his work for school.
lessons.text:
Tom has some work for school. He does not know how to do it. He says to his sister, Ella: "Ella, can you do this with me? I don't know it."

Ella says: "I can. If you want, I will look at it. Could you give me your work?"

Tom gives Ella his work. She looks at it. She says: "Your work is good. If you do this one that way, it will be right."

Tom does it. Now it is right. He says: "Could you look at one more? I don't know that one."

Ella says: "I would, but I think you can do it now. Would you like to do it?"

Tom does it. It is right! He says: "I can do it because you are with me."

Ella says: "You can do it because you are good at it."

Questions:
What does Tom have?
Tom has some work for school.
What does Tom say to Ella?
He says: "Can you do this with me?"
Can Tom do it now?
Tom can do it now.

lessons.title: A Day at the Park
lessons.summary: Anna takes her two children to the park for the day.
lessons.text:
It is a good day. Anna wants to take her two children, Sara and Jim, out for the day.

Anna says: "How about the park? We can go there for some time."

Sara says: "We can take the ball!" Jim says: "Or we can take some other things."

Anna says: "The ball is good for the park, but we don't need other things."

They go to the park. Sara and Jim run with the ball. Jim is as good with it as Sara. Anna looks at them. She thinks about how good the day is.

When the day is over, they go back. Sara says: "It was a good day, but when can we come back?"

Questions:
Who does Anna take out for the day?
Anna takes Sara and Jim.
What does Sara want to take?
Sara wants to take the ball.
Do they take the ball or other things?
They take the ball.
What do Sara and Jim do there?
They run with the ball.
What does Anna think about?
She thinks about how good the day is.
